title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-03-21
content:
Summary
This weekly SRE update covers incidents from 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-20, SLO status, on-call handoffs, outstanding action items, and decisions from the 2026-03-20 weekly SRE sync. High level: two incidents with customer impact (INC-2026-03-18-1 and INC-2026-03-19-2). We are slightly behind our monthly availability/SLO targets and have prioritized three follow-up fixes to prevent recurrence.

Incidents
1) INC-2026-03-18-1 \u2014 Elevated error rate on model-serving gateway
- Window: 2026-03-18 06:40 - 07:15 PST
- Impact: 4% of requests returned 5xx, partial degradation for hosted-api customers in us-west region. No data loss. Some customers experienced increased client retries and higher latency.
- Root cause (initial): Regression in the custom autoscaler introduced during the 2026-03-17 deploy that under-provisioned endpoints under a short traffic spike. The autoscaler incorrectly used a smoothed metric that lagged and failed to scale quickly.
- Mitigation: Rolled back autoscaler config to previous stable version at 06:52 PST and applied temporary override to increase min replicas for critical routes. Hotfix PR merged to revert smoothing change.
- Post-incident status: Full service restored by 07:15 PST. Postmortem drafted and linked (see linked_artifacts).
- Action items from INC-2026-03-18-1: SRE-342 (Jira) created for the long-term fix to autoscaler logic; add e2e autoscaler test that simulates rapid traffic spikes; add an alert for sustained \"autoscaler-activity < expected\" state. Owners: Daniel Kim (fix) due 2026-04-02; Priya Desai (e2e test) due 2026-03-30.

2) INC-2026-03-19-2 \u2014 KV cache warmup delays causing high p95 latency for cold routes
- Window: 2026-03-19 14:05 - 14:45 PST
- Impact: Cold-start latency increased for some model variants, p95 spiked from baseline ~180ms to ~420ms for affected shards. Affected primarily dedicated pools with recent scaling events.
- Mitigation: Executed targeted cache-warm script to pre-populate KV caches for recently scaled replicas, and temporarily increased pre-warm concurrency. Latency returned to baseline by 14:45 PST.
- Root cause (investigation ongoing): Longer-than-expected block on background prewarm due to a scheduling regression in the cache-warm worker introduced by a thread-pool change (linked to diff in infra repo).
- Post-incident status: Running additional validation; formal postmortem pending.
- Action items: Add integration test for cache-warm worker under scale-up conditions (owner: Ethan Zhang due 2026-04-06); add dashboard panels for cache-warm job latency and queue length (owner: Rosa Martinez due 2026-03-28).

SLOs and Metrics
- Monthly availability SLO for serving runtime: target 99.95%. Current month-to-date (Mar 1 - Mar 21): 99.93% (two incidents drove most of the delta).
- Alerting: We hit the paging threshold for availability on 2026-03-18 and 2026-03-19 which triggered on-call pages as expected.
- Latency targets: p95 target = 200ms (global). Measured p95 for the week: 210ms (short-term spike due to cache warm and autoscaler lag).
- Error budget: Remaining error budget for March: ~0.02% -> elevated risk for new risky changes. Recommend holding non-critical deploys until fixes are in place or canary windows extended.

On-call handoffs and rota
- Current rotation (week of 2026-03-14 -> 2026-03-21):
  - Primary: Aisha Patel (on-call owner)
  - Secondary: Daniel Kim
  - Pager duty notes: Primary received 3 pages (2 incidents + 1 noisy alert) this week.
- Next rotation (week starting 2026-03-21):
  - Primary: Rosa Martinez
  - Secondary: Ethan Zhang
- Handoff checklist items completed: verified runbooks for gateway autoscaler and cache warm, checked runbook ownership, validated escalation contacts.

Weekly SRE sync (2026-03-20) \u2014 notes & decisions
- Attendees: Aisha, Daniel, Rosa, Ethan, Priya, infra eng lead (Samir)
- Key discussion points:
  - Autoscaler regression review: agreed to pause any further smoothing-related optimizations until autoscaler e2e tests are added.
  - Cache warm: infra team will add visibility metrics and a synthetic that fires after scale events to validate warm progress.
  - SLO posture: because we are nearing our error budget limit for March, we will: 1) set a temporary freeze on non-essential model-variant rollouts, 2) extend canary windows for infra changes to 48 hours where possible.
- Decisions made:
  - Create an \"SRE safety freeze\" label for PRs that are non-critical; repo admins will delay mergers that don't have SRE signoff. (Owner: Samir; due 2026-03-24)
  - Increase default min replicas for hosted-api critical routes to reduce sensitivity to autoscaler lag (Owner: Priya; due 2026-03-25).

Ongoing projects / work in progress
- Runbook refresh: updating the gateway autoscaler and cache-warm runbooks with clearer escalation paths and play-by-play mitigations. (Owner: Aisha; due 2026-03-29)
- Observability upgrade: scheduled maintenance to upgrade tracing backend and agent on 2026-03-24 01:00-03:00 UTC. Expect short-lived metric ingest lag; will not affect serving runtime but may delay alerting. (Owner: Rosa; change ticket: OPS-657)
- Load testing: plan to run a nationally distributed load test on 2026-04-02 to validate autoscaler and cache warm behavior under peak traffic. (Owner: Daniel; test runbook: LT-AUTOSCALER-2026-04-02)

Action items (high priority)
- SRE-342: Fix autoscaler smoothing regression + add e2e autoscaler test. Owner: Daniel Kim. Due: 2026-04-02.
- Add cache-warm worker integration test and dashboard panels. Owner: Ethan Zhang & Rosa Martinez. Due: 2026-04-06 / 2026-03-28.
- Create SRE safety freeze label & PR workflow. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-24.
- Increase min replicas for critical hosted-api routes. Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2026-03-25.
- Runbook refresh for autoscaler and cache-warm. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-29.

Blockers / Needs
- Need infra team's review and signoff on proposed autoscaler fix before merging. Requesting expedited code review: PR #INFRA-2045.
- Observability upgrade requires temporary on-call coverage to watch for missed alerts during the 2026-03-24 window. Sign-up sheet on Slack #sre-ops.

Notes to leadership
- We are currently slightly below our monthly availability SLO due to two operational incidents. The root causes are identified and limited in scope. The main risk area is the autoscaler and its sensitivity to smoothing under rapid traffic changes; we recommend prioritizing SRE-342 and the e2e tests.
- If leadership plans any high-traffic marketing or customer demos in the next two weeks, inform SRE so we can schedule extra capacity and monitoring.

Appendix / Links referenced in doc
- INC-2026-03-18-1 postmortem (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-03-18-1
- INC-2026-03-19-2 incident notes (work-in-progress): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-03-19-2
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-342
- Runbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SRE+Runbooks

If there are urgent follow-ups not captured above, annotate this doc or ping the on-call channel.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (SRE Lead)
Reviewers: Daniel Kim, Rosa Martinez, Ethan Zhang
